page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.16xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and AWS Graviton architecture. It features a 64-core ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz, where each vCPU maps directly to a dedicated physical core without simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 128.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per core ratio aligned with compute-intensive requirements. Bundled hardware includes 3800 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage and a 25 Gbps baseline network bandwidth interface, with no GPU hardware present.

Performance benchmarks demonstrate significant multi-core scalability and high memory subsystem speeds for cached data. The instance achieved 97,024.22 in stress-ng multi-core testing and demonstrated strong build performance with a Clang compilation score of 43,397.0. Data-serving benchmarks show 73.0 million Redis SET operations per second alongside 45.02 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. Tradeoffs are evident in single-core performance, where Geekbench single-core scored 973.0, and in LLM token generation speeds which remain modest on this architecture.

The combination of 64 dedicated ARM cores and direct-attached NVMe storage delivers high resource density for parallel tasks requiring fast scratch disk access. By avoiding hyperthreading contention, execution remains consistent across heavily loaded threads. The instance is well-matched for distributed caching, high-concurrency web serving, CI/CD build environments, batch data processing, and large-scale software compilation jobs compiled for the arm64 architecture.

Driven by the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the platform provides a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation without simultaneous multithreading, supplemented by 25 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark testing reflects strong multi-threaded execution, producing 97,024.22 on stress-ng multi-core, 43,397.0 in Clang software compilation, and 73.0 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread benchmarks demonstrate lower relative execution marks, the substantial core count and integrated high-speed local disk capacity offer efficient throughput for parallelized architectures. The system is suited for CI/CD compilation farms, static web hosting, Redis caching layers, and high-concurrency data engineering workloads.
